surface_leak: A density-increment iteration with the same shape as the cap-set argument.
why_negative: SALEM-SPENCER 1942 constructed 3AP-free subsets of [N] of density exp(-log N/log log N), showing the true order of r_3(N) exceeds N^{1-eps} for every fixed eps > 0. That exclusion of power savings is what N3 asserts, and it is Salem-Spencer's, not Behrend's. BEHREND 1946 gives the stronger and still essentially best-known lower bound r_3(N) = Omega(N/exp(C sqrt(log N))). The cap-set after-board does not transfer.

sources.cite: Salem, Spencer 1942 -- the exclusion of power savings
sources.role: states the consequence N3 asserts, outright
sources.basis: Row N3 RE-ATTRIBUTED the exclusion of power savings to Salem-Spencer 1942, from the Peluse transcript. This is the half the item leans on.

sources.cite: Behrend 1946 -- the best known lower bound
sources.role: stronger bound; the exclusion does not need it
sources.basis: Rows N3 and N3-behrend-improvements: Behrend 1946 is the stronger, still essentially best-known bound, with small improvements by Elkin 2011 and Green-Wolf 2010 from the Bloom-Sisask reference list.

asymptotic_only.statement: The exclusion is ASYMPTOTIC. Behrend's set exceeds N^{1-delta} only past a crossover, and the crossover is large.
asymptotic_only.derivation: c = 2*sqrt(2)*sqrt(ln 2) = 2.3548; need ln N > (c/delta)^2. Verified in tools/check_citations_response.py.

decay_watch: arXiv:2406.12290 (June 2024) is the FIRST quasipolynomial improvement to Behrend since 1946. It does NOT change N3's status -- a quasipolynomial improvement to a sub-power-saving bound is still sub-power-saving -- but it is the class of event that moved Erdos distinct distances in R^3 into REJECTED.json. Re-check the other twins for movement.
